findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket (which holds report data and a seeded vendor roster) are not guaranteed to be encrypted with a managed key.
The bucket defines no ACL and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so bucket/object ACLs or policies could make the reports data publicly readable or writable.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to report objects would leave no S3 server access log trail for forensic review.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be permanently deleted or overwritten by an attacker with write access with no recovery path.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial ledger data stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for this ledger bucket, so access to sensitive financial exports is not audited.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so ledger export objects can be irrecoverably deleted or tampered with.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts this bucket, so a future ACL or policy change could expose the ledger data publicly.
The model artifacts bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so proprietary model data is stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No public access block is associated with this bucket, leaving it open to accidental public exposure via ACL or bucket policy changes.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks frequently contain sensitive procedures, hostnames, and credentials stored unencrypted.
No logging block is defined, so access to operational runbooks is not recorded in any server access log.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against ACLs or policies that grant public access.
The audit trail bucket, which receives logs from other buckets, has no logging configuration of its own, so tampering with or reading of audit logs is itself unaudited.
force_destroy is true and no object lock / MFA delete is configured on the audit log bucket, allowing an attacker or careless operator to destroy the audit trail and its evidence.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so audit logs could be exposed publicly through an ACL or policy misconfiguration.

The vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded without specifying server_side_encryption or kms_key_id into a bucket that has no default encryption, so this potentially sensitive vendor data is stored in plaintext.
